question: What is the primary purpose of the Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in healthcare institutions?

options.A: To generate personal profits for hospital management staff
options.B: To ensure continuous and sustainable availability of affordable essential medicines
options.C: To completely replace government funding for all hospital infrastructure
options.D: To provide free medical care indefinitely without any financial contribution

explanation: The core purpose of the DRF is to establish a self-sustaining cycle that ensures essential medicines remain continuously available and affordable to patients. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h1)

question: How is the DRF typically initiated in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Through continuous borrowing from commercial banks at high interest rates
options.B: Through voluntary donations from individual nursing staff members
options.C: Through an initial seed capital provided by government, donors, or grants
options.D: Through mandatory deductions from patients' personal salaries

explanation: A DRF starts with an initial seed capital or grant to procure the first batch of essential medicines, which then funds subsequent restocking through sales revenue. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h1)

question: What does the principle of ring-fencing mean in the context of the Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Drug revenues can be used to pay any hospital utility bill
options.B: Monies generated from drug sales must only be reinvested into restocking drugs
options.C: Pharmacies must be physically fenced off from the main hospital building
options.D: Only senior medical doctors can authorize spending from the fund

explanation: Ring-fencing ensures that DRF revenue is strictly reserved for purchasing more medications and is not diverted to other hospital expenses. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h2)

question: Why are DRF drugs priced slightly above cost price rather than given away completely free or sold at high market rates?

options.A: To generate massive wealth for the hospital board of directors
options.B: To account for inflation, shipping, and sustainable restocking while remaining affordable
options.C: To discourage patients from buying too many medications at once
options.D: To pay the salaries of administrative nursing personnel

explanation: A slight markup covers operational realities like inflation and restocking expenses, ensuring the fund can continuously purchase new inventory. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h2)

question: Who typically forms the oversight committee for a healthcare facility's Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Only external auditors from international organizations
options.B: A multidisciplinary team including pharmacists, accountants, and clinicians
options.C: Patient representatives and local community leaders only
options.D: The hospital security guards and gatekeepers

explanation: A multidisciplinary committee of healthcare professionals and finance experts ensures balanced oversight of both clinical and financial aspects of the DRF. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why must a DRF maintain a dedicated bank account separate from the hospital's general account?

options.A: To make auditing easier and prevent unauthorized diversion of funds
options.B: Because commercial banks require separate accounts for medical staff
options.C: To prevent patients from knowing how much money the hospital makes
options.D: To allow nurses to withdraw cash for personal emergencies

explanation: A separate, dedicated account ensures transparent tracking of drug revenues and prevents funds from being mistakenly used for non-pharmaceutical expenses. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of using the FEFO (First-Expired, First-Out) inventory method in a DRF warehouse?

options.A: To ensure that the most expensive drugs are sold first
options.B: To minimize financial losses caused by drug expiration
options.C: To make warehouse shelves look neat and organized
options.D: To comply with international fashion standards

explanation: FEFO ensures that products expiring sooner are dispensed first, preventing financial loss and wastage from expired stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why is procurement in a DRF restricted to reputable manufacturers and regulatory-approved vendors?

options.A: To prevent the infiltration of sub-standard and falsified medicines
options.B: To ensure that the hospital receives cash kickbacks
options.C: Because local vendors are legally not allowed to sell tablets
options.D: To make the procurement process as slow and difficult as possible

explanation: Sourcing from approved vendors safeguards patient safety by ensuring that all supplied drugs are genuine, safe, and efficacious. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the primary threat to the sustainability of a Drug Revolving Fund over time?

options.A: Patients taking their medications exactly as prescribed
options.B: Inflation, uncollected debts, pilferage, and poor inventory control
options.C: Nurses writing too many accurate patient care reports
options.D: Having too many active pharmaceutical suppliers

explanation: Factors like inflation, unpaid patient debts, theft, and holding unsellable stock erode the fund's capital and cause it to collapse. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h5)

question: How should drug prices generally be calculated in a sustainable DRF model?

options.A: By matching the highest prices charged by private luxury hospitals
options.B: By charging random amounts based on how a patient looks
options.C: Using a transparent markup formula that covers procurement costs and a small buffer
options.D: By offering all medications completely free of charge indefinitely

explanation: A transparent markup covers operational realities and restocking expenses while keeping prices significantly lower than the open market. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h5)

question: How do nurses contribute directly to inventory stewardship within the ward setting?

options.A: By ordering massive quantities of drugs without doctor approval
options.B: By monitoring treatment rooms for near-expiry drugs and reporting stock-outs
options.C: By selling surplus medications to patients for personal cash
options.D: By taking over full management of the hospital central pharmacy

explanation: Nurses help manage inventory by watching for near-expiry items in wards and reporting shortages so the pharmacy can restock promptly. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is an important role of the nurse regarding patient education and the DRF?

options.A: Teaching patients about the importance of purchasing authentic drugs from the hospital pharmacy
options.B: Convincing patients to buy cheaper fake drugs from roadside vendors
options.C: Explaining how hospital accountants calculate inflation markups
options.D: Negotiating wholesale prices directly with international manufacturers

explanation: Nurses educate patients on compliance and the importance of obtaining safe, genuine medications from the accredited facility pharmacy. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h6)

question: How does macroeconomic instability, such as severe currency devaluation, impact a DRF?

options.A: It automatically doubles the physical number of drugs in the warehouse
options.B: It reduces the purchasing power of the fund, making restocking difficult
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to give drugs away for free
options.D: It eliminates all forms of corruption within the hospital

explanation: Devaluation and inflation erode the fund's capital value, meaning the accumulated cash can no longer buy the same quantity of drugs. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is a major consequence of weak internal controls and staff corruption in a DRF scheme?

options.A: Rapid capital depletion and sudden stock-outs of essential medicines
options.B: Increased trust from international donor agencies
options.C: Faster delivery of high-quality pharmaceuticals from abroad
options.D: Better health outcomes and lower mortality rates for patients

explanation: Theft, embezzlement, and poor oversight drain the financial resources of the fund, resulting in severe drug shortages. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is the benefit of digitizing the pharmacy inventory and supply chain in a DRF system?

options.A: It eliminates manual errors, improves tracking, and helps curb pilferage
options.B: It removes the need for any human staff members in the hospital
options.C: It allows nurses to automatically prescribe medications independently
options.D: It ensures that medicines never expire under any circumstances

explanation: Digital systems streamline tracking, reduce human calculation errors, and provide better security against theft and inventory discrepancies. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h8)

question: Which of the following represents a key performance indicator (KPI) used to monitor a DRF?

options.A: The number of flowers planted outside the hospital entrance
options.B: Stock-out frequency and inventory turnover rate
options.C: The average height and weight of incoming nursing students
options.D: The personal salary of the hospital accountant

explanation: Tracking how often items go out of stock and how quickly inventory turns over are critical metrics for evaluating DRF performance. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T1#GNS215_U3_T1_h8)
